propositions: Sandbox enforcement tests pass when the sandbox fails to launch because they only assert the absence of a file without verifying the sandboxed child actually executed
The tests lack a liveness check that proves the child reached its write attempt before the denial was enforced
A total sandbox launch failure (bad profile, missing binary, namespace refusal) produces the same file-absent state as successful enforcement, making the test pass incorrectly
Acceptance criteria require each enforcement test to assert positive liveness through an artifact produced by the child after starting, not through exit status
The incident-shape deletion test must be bounded to prevent escaping the pytest tmp directory even if sandbox enforcement completely fails
